transcript:
[00:00] Sophie Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Sophie from Redwood, I'll hand it off to Diego for a quick demo and then we'll chat about the PoC.
[00:12] Diego Ramos: Great, hi Maya, Tom, Priya, thanks for the time. Quick agenda: embeddings generation, candidate retrieval, then our reranking endpoint and how that integrates into a search stack, then the Console and Optimize suggestions.
[00:29] Maya Chen: Sounds good. We're mostly interested in improving relevance for product search — short queries, a lot of SKU-level items. Latency's important, can't add more than ~100ms extra on the critical path.
[00:40] Sophie Patel: Got it. Also wanted to confirm constraints: data residency? compliance?
[00:44] Maya Chen: We need SOC 2 and SSO with Okta, and anything stored longer than 30 days must be approved by legal.
[00:53] Diego Ramos: Perfect, we support SAML SSO and have SOC 2 docs — we'll share them after. Also data retention via the Console, you can set automatic purge or opt to not persist embeddings.
[01:06] Tom Alvarez: How do we do the rerank — do you expect us to store document embeddings?
[01:10] Diego Ramos: You can either precompute and store doc embeddings in your vector DB (we see customers use Faiss, Milvus, Pinecone) and then call our rerank endpoint which accepts a query embedding plus the candidate doc text or doc embeddings. The reranker is optimized for short candidate lists — think top 50 candidates.
[01:27] Priya Nair: Do you support reranking with dense + sparse hybrid? Like BM25 + dense rerank?
[01:31] Diego Ramos: Yes, common pattern is BM25 or Elastic for initial retrieval, then dense rerank. We also have a sample pipeline in the docs. One caveat: if you pass doc embeddings directly to rerank, you save tokenization and reduce latency.
[01:44] Speaker 2: (background) mm-hmm.
[01:55] Diego Ramos: I'm going to switch to the demo — Console screen share.
[02:02] Diego Ramos: Here is the Embeddings API docs — it's a single endpoint POST /v1/embeddings, you can pass batching of up to N inputs per request, we recommend batching for bulk jobs but single-request for low-latency per-query.
[02:22] Diego Ramos: Example: POST with 512-d vectors (depending on model) — dimension depends on model family. We show the model's dims in the catalog.
[02:35] Priya Nair: What models do you host for embeddings?
[02:38] Diego Ramos: We have curated open models: ada-style 1536, some LLM-derived dense embeddings, and Redwood-verified model profiles. If you want larger vector dims for semantic nuances we can recommend those in Optimize.
[02:54] Maya Chen: Latency — for a single query embedding call, what's typical?
[02:59] Diego Ramos: For hosted API small models: 20–40ms p95 for embedding generation in our US region, bigger models up to ~120ms. If you precompute doc embeddings, the rerank step is often dominated by the reranker cost and any text tokenization; passing doc embeddings avoids that.
[03:15] Tom Alvarez: If we do rerank with docs as text, will you tokenize and run the model on your side?
[03:20] Diego Ramos: Yes, we will re-encode the doc text client-side or server-side depending on the call — there's an option to send doc embeddings to skip that. Tokenization adds latency and cost.
[03:31] Diego Ramos: Now I'll demo the reranking endpoint — POST /v1/rerank. You send the query (text or embedding) and candidate docs; response is scores and reordered list plus explanation tokens if you enable structured output.
[03:47] Maya Chen: Explanation tokens?
[03:49] Diego Ramos: It's a structured output mode where we return a short rationale and token-level highlights, useful for logging and quality checks. It costs more tokens but helps debug relevance regressions.
[04:02] Priya Nair: Can we run rerank in streaming mode? We need to show partial results in UI sometimes.
[04:07] Diego Ramos: Rerank is synchronous, but we provide streaming for generation endpoints; for rerank we typically return the full ranked list. You can combine with a client-side progressive display while we compute the full rerank.
[04:22] Sophie Patel: Two operational notes — quota/rate limits are per-API key, and you can create multiple keys in the Console for different services; Dedicated customers can get higher reserved throughput.
[04:36] Tom Alvarez: What's the cost split — do you bill embeddings separately from rerank?
[04:41] Sophie Patel: Yes, embeddings are per-embedding-unit (per input token/embedding request) and rerank is per-token consumed by the reranker model. In the Console you can see token-level cost per route. We'll include pricing examples in the follow-up.
[04:55] Diego Ramos: Switching to a small live demo — I'll send a query for "wireless barcode scanner" and show top-k retrieval then rerank.
[05:07] Diego Ramos: (typing) First we call our embeddings endpoint for the query, then we do cosine search in Faiss (local example) to get top 50 candidates, then call /v1/rerank with the query embedding and candidate doc embeddings.
[05:27] Diego Ramos: (demo) Ok results came back — you can see reordering: previously product A at pos 5 moved to pos 1 after rerank because of attribute match.
[05:39] Maya Chen: Nice — can you show the Console trace for that request?
[05:42] Diego Ramos: Yep, trace view shows per-route latency 86ms, model latency 45ms, tokenization 12ms, and caching hit 0%. We also have a token cost breakdown: embeddings cost $X per request and rerank cost $Y.
[05:58] Priya Nair: What's KV cash? I saw that in the docs — is that the same as KV cache?
[06:02] Diego Ramos: That's a typo in the auto transcript, KV cache — it's our prefix cache for common prompt fragments; helps reduce cost on repeated contexts.
[06:12] Tom Alvarez: For our throughput, we have bursts during promo windows — can Redwood handle sudden spikes?
[06:17] Sophie Patel: For Hosted API we have autoscaling and burst windows, but for predictable high throughput we'd recommend Dedicated. We can model your traffic and give guidance.
[06:29] Maya Chen: Are there any concerns about passing PII in embeddings? We need guarantees.
[06:34] Sophie Patel: Hosted API has optional no-persist mode; embeddings can be configured not to be stored. We also support customer-managed keys (KMS) and have audit logs. We'll send the SOC 2 + KMS integration doc.
[06:48] Diego Ramos: Back to rerank: we tune the reranker temperature and similarity thresholds; we also support learning-to-rank features where you can pass numeric signals along with text.
[07:01] Priya Nair: How do we evaluate quality? Do you have suggestion on eval harness or integration with Redwood Optimize?
[07:06] Diego Ramos: Yes, Optimize provides automatic A/B comparisons, prompt-set based evals, and regression alerts. We'll pull a baseline for your sample queries and show a precision@k delta.
[07:19] Sophie Patel: Quick Q — any legal or procurement timeline?
[07:22] Maya Chen: We aim to run a two-week PoC by end of month, procurement signs off in about 3–4 weeks.
[07:30] Diego Ramos: Great — I'll demo a couple more features: the embedding bulk upload, and the per-route dashboards for rerank.
[07:40] Diego Ramos: In Console you can pin a model version so production uses the same weights. If you want to experiment, we recommend canary rollouts.
[07:51] Tom Alvarez: Does Canary mean you use 10% of traffic on a new model?
[07:54] Diego Ramos: Exactly, and you can set automatic rollback thresholds if latency or error rates spike.
[08:02] Maya Chen: Any integrations with our existing Elastic cluster?
[08:05] Diego Ramos: We have examples: use Elastic/BM25 as retriever, call embeddings for rerank; we also have connectors to push embeddings into Elastic's vector field.
[08:17] Priya Nair: For the PoC, we'd probably want to run on a subset of SKUs — maybe two categories. Can you help size cost for that?
[08:25] Sophie Patel: We'll send a cost estimate based on the query/QPS and document corpus size.
[08:30] Diego Ramos: One more demo — Optimize suggestions: it recommended quantizing a particular model from fp16 to int8 for 2x cost reduction while keeping p95 latency under target for your workload. This is model dependent.
[08:47] Maya Chen: Do we lose relevance when quantizing?
[08:50] Diego Ramos: Usually small degradation in some edge cases; Optimize can run a small eval on your held-out prompts and report expected delta.
[09:00] Sophie Patel: We're nearing the end; quick recap and next steps.
[09:05] Maya Chen: Quick question — what's the expected p95 for rerank on 50 candidates?
[09:10] Diego Ramos: If you're passing embeddings for candidates, 30–60ms p95 in hosted us-west. If you pass raw text it can go up by 50–120ms depending on doc length.
[09:22] Tom Alvarez: For the PoC we'll precompute doc embeddings and only call query embedding + rerank.
[09:28] Sophie Patel: Perfect, recap of next steps: 1) Redwood to send pricing and SOC 2 + KMS docs, 2) Redwood SE to run a quick benchmark plan and template, 3) schedule a 30-min integration kickoff next week.
[09:43] Priya Nair: Can you share the demo script and the Faiss toy code?
[09:48] Diego Ramos: Yes, I'll drop the sample repo and a notebook.
[09:53] Maya Chen: Great — thanks, this was useful.
[09:57] Sophie Patel: Thanks all. We'll follow up via email with links.
[10:02] (call ends)
